newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Ilyushin sees Il-96T first flight in 96.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Ilyushin sees Il-96T first flight in 96.

text.p: Russia's Ilyushin design bureau hopes its new Il-96T freighter aircraft will have its first test flight this year despite cash problems hampering the project, an Ilyushin official said on Monday.
Chief designer Genrikh Novozhilov told Reuters that the Il-96T, which is powered by U.S. engines and avionics, was almost ready for its first test flight.
"I hope it will make the first flight by the end of this year," Novozhilov said.

But he said some Russian firms have refused to supply essential parts for the jet because Ilyushin and its partner in the project, the Voronezh aviation factory, do not have enough money to pay for them.
A Voronezh official confirmed that the plant had financial difficulties.
"They do not want to understand that the faster we begin to sell the aircraft, the faster we will start making money," Novozhilov said.
The Il-96T jet is powered by four engines from Pratt and Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corporation, and has avionics from Rockwell International.
Both the U.S. companies have already supplied the equipment for the prototype, paid for by the U.S. government, an Ilyushin spokesman said.
Ilyushin and Voronezh planned the Il-96T plane's first test flight for April this year, but it was postponed several times because of a lack of cash.
The plane has two cargo decks that can carry 50 tonnes over 11,000 km (6,875 miles) or 92 tonnes over 5,000 km (3,125 miles).
Ilyushin hopes to certify the plane in Russia and the United States.

Novozhilov also said that Russia's flagship carrier Aeroflot Russian International Airlines had confirmed a $1.5 billion deal to buy 17 Il-96M passenger jets and three Il-96T freighters. Aeroflot originally signed the contract in 1995, but ordered 10 passenger and 10 cargo jets.
